title: Best Line at a Point

source.name: Original exercise; classic technique (Li Chao tree)

statement:
You maintain a set of lines `y = m * x + b`. Process `q` operations:

- `1 m b`: add the line `y = m * x + b` to the set (lines may have equal slopes; they are all kept).
- `2 x`: print the **largest value** of `m * x + b` over all lines currently in the set, at the integer point `x`.

There is at least one line in the set before every query of type 2.

**Input.** The first line holds `q`; then `q` lines, each an operation.

**Output.** One line for every query of type 2.
constraints: |m|, |b| ≤ 10^6 and |x| ≤ 10^6, so every value m * x + b fits in 64 bits (and in a JavaScript Number)
hints: Evaluating every line for every query is O(q^2). The convex hull trick keeps the upper envelope of the lines in a sorted structure, but inserting a line with an arbitrary slope in the middle is awkward.

Use a segment tree over the possible x values where each node stores one line, the one that is best at the node's midpoint. When a new line arrives, compare it with the stored line at the midpoint: the winner stays; the loser can win on at most one of the two halves, so pass it down to that half only.

A query walks from the root to the leaf of x, evaluating the line stored in every node on the way, and keeps the maximum. Both operations take O(log range) steps, and nodes can be created only when needed.
editorial: A **Li Chao tree** is a segment tree over the domain of query points (here the integers from `-10^6` to `10^6`) in which every node stores **at most one line**. The invariant: for any `x`, the best line at `x` is stored in some node on the path from the root to the leaf of `x`. To insert a line, start at the root and compare the new line with the stored one **at the midpoint** `mid` of the node's interval; the line that is better there stays in the node and the other one continues. Two distinct lines cross at most once, so the loser can be better than the winner on at most one of the two halves: if it beats the stored line at the left end it can only win on the left half (go left), else if it beats it at the right end it can only win on the right half (go right), otherwise it is dominated on the whole interval and is discarded. When the child does not exist yet, create it holding the loser and stop. Because every insertion either terminates or moves one level down, it costs `O(log C)` where `C` is the size of the domain, and a dynamic tree has at most one node per inserted line. A query at `x` walks down the root-to-leaf path, evaluates the stored line in each node and takes the maximum, also `O(log C)`. Compared with the classic convex hull trick (see the DP lesson), the Li Chao tree needs no monotonicity of slopes or of query points and handles arbitrary insertion order; with a different comparison it also supports minimum queries, and line segments restricted to an interval. The largest values are about `2 * 10^12`, safe in 64-bit integers and in doubles; use a larger domain by compressing the offline query points.

solutions.python:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
q = int(data[0])
LO, HI = -10**6, 10**6                      # the range of query points
slope, icpt, left, right = [], [], [], []   # a dynamic Li Chao tree: each node keeps one line
def add(m, b):
    if not slope:
        slope.append(m); icpt.append(b); left.append(-1); right.append(-1)
        return
    node, lo, hi = 0, LO, HI
    while True:
        mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
        if m * mid + b > slope[node] * mid + icpt[node]:       # the new line is better at the midpoint: it takes the node
            slope[node], m = m, slope[node]
            icpt[node], b = b, icpt[node]
        if lo == hi:
            return
        if m * lo + b > slope[node] * lo + icpt[node]:         # the line that lost can still win on the left half
            nxt, hi = left, mid
            side = left
        elif m * hi + b > slope[node] * hi + icpt[node]:       # or on the right half
            lo = mid + 1
            side = right
        else:
            return                                             # it loses everywhere: discard it
        if side[node] == -1:
            slope.append(m); icpt.append(b); left.append(-1); right.append(-1)
            side[node] = len(slope) - 1
            return
        node = side[node]
def query(x):
    node, lo, hi = 0, LO, HI
    best = None
    while node != -1:
        v = slope[node] * x + icpt[node]
        if best is None or v > best:
            best = v
        mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
        if x <= mid:
            node, hi = left[node], mid
        else:
            node, lo = right[node], mid + 1
    return best
out = []
pos = 1
for _ in range(q):
    if data[pos] == '1':
        add(int(data[pos + 1]), int(data[pos + 2]))
        pos += 3
    else:
        out.append(query(int(data[pos + 1])))
        pos += 2
print("\n".join(map(str, out)))
